I am an 18-year-old girl farming here in Zomba, and this small bean plot of 0.09 hectares is intercropped with our other crops. We do not have coupons for fertilizer on beans—FISP is mainly for maize—and besides, beans fix their own nitrogen from the air, so I will not waste money on chemical fertilizer. I will put some composted manure from our animals on the plot, and I will plant the bean seeds we saved from last season rather than buying new ones. My mother, sisters, and I will do all the planting, weeding, and harvesting ourselves because the plot is small and we cannot afford to hire anyone.
